text: Question: Why is my FTTH broadband connection showing 'LOS' (Loss of Signal) on the ONT? Answer: ### Short Answer An LOS/red light usually indicates a fibre cut, a loose connector at the ONT, or an upstream outage. Check that the fibre cable is firmly connected; if the light remains red, log a fault ticket — do not attempt to open the ONT casing yourself. ### Detailed Explanation The three possible causes are ordered from most to least customer-fixable: a loose connector (something the customer can check safely), a fibre cut or upstream outage (both outside the customer's control) — and the explicit warning not to open the ONT casing draws a clear line around what's safe for the customer to attempt versus what requires a technician. ### Key Details | Detail | Value | |---|---| | Possible causes | Fibre cut; loose connector at the ONT; upstream outage | | Customer-safe check | Confirm fibre cable is firmly connected | | If light remains red | Log a fault ticket | | Explicit warning | Do not open the ONT casing yourself | ### Troubleshooting | Symptom | Possible Cause | Diagnostic Check | Recommended Action | |---|---|---|---| | LOS light on, cable appears loose | Loose connector at the ONT | Physical connection at the ONT | Firmly reseat the fibre cable connector | | LOS light stays red after reseating cable | Fibre cut or upstream outage | Whether other customers nearby are also affected (informal signal of
title: Why is my FTTH broadband connection showing 'LOS' (Loss of Signal) on the ONT?
